features.title: Intermediate Artifact Lifecycle and Cleanup
features.description: Keep Bronze/Silver/Gold artifacts available long enough for recovery, audit and retry, then reclaim them after the Final artifact and registry are safely committed. Cleanup must never run before Save has established the final persistence boundary. Draft abandonment and temporary object retention are handled explicitly rather than through ad-hoc deletion.

tasks.title: Define configurable retention policy for draft, Bronze, Silver and Gold artifacts; FINAL artifacts are retained according to dataset lifecycle rather than intermediate cleanup
tasks.result: apps/backend/src/config/env.config.ts: CLEANUP_DRAFT_RECOVERY_HOURS and CLEANUP_INTERMEDIATE_RETENTION_HOURS (both default 168h/7d). Two windows, not one -- they gate two different eligibility paths (see T05/T02). Verified live against real Postgres (see V01 note below): seeding a draft with updatedAt 200h in the past correctly crossed the default window; 1h in the past correctly did not.

tasks.title: After successful Save, mark the draft adopted and make its artifacts eligible for lifecycle cleanup without copying or rewriting the FINAL artifact
tasks.result: Already satisfied by pre-existing code, not new work: saveDraftAsDatasetService's $transaction (dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts:777-780) writes {savedDatasetId, status:'SAVED'} on the draft at Save time, which is exactly the adoption signal selectCleanupEligibleArtifacts' SAVED branch reads. No FINAL artifact is copied or rewritten; the draft transitioning to SAVED is what makes its non-adopted BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD siblings eligible once their window elapses.

tasks.title: Add safe cleanup worker/job that verifies artifact ownership, adoption state, retention age and absence of active jobs before deletion
tasks.result: ArtifactCleanupAdminService (apps/backend/src/api/v1/artifact-cleanup/admin/) verifies, per artifact: ownership (via draftId -> DatasetDraft lookup), adoption state (draft.status), retention age (selectCleanupEligibleArtifacts), lineage-pin (protectedArtifactIds), and absence of an active QUEUED/RUNNING PreprocessingJob referencing it as source or result. Unit-tested (8 cases, artifact-cleanup.admin.service.spec.ts) and verified live against real Postgres: an artifact referenced by a real RUNNING job row was correctly excluded (see V02 note).

tasks.title: Configure MinIO lifecycle rules for eligible temporary/intermediate object prefixes where the retention model can be expressed safely; application-level cleanup remains the authority when reference checks are required
tasks.result: ObjectStore.ensure_tmp_lifecycle_rule() (apps/python/intergrations/object_store.py) configures a bucket-wide MinIO lifecycle rule (7-day expiry) matched by an object TAG (lifecycle=tmp) rather than a Prefix filter, because tmp/ lives under a per-dataset prefix that no single literal Prefix can match across datasets. put_frame() tags every tmp/ write; committed artifact writes are never tagged. Verified LIVE against the real minio-local container: rule created, re-run confirmed idempotent (no duplicate rule, exact expected expiration days), tmp write carried the tag, committed-artifact write did not. Backstop only -- PreprocessingJobService's existing /cleanup call remains the primary, prompt path. Deliberately no automatic runtime caller (matches ensure_bucket()'s own established precedent) -- run once per environment as an explicit ops step; wiring it into every app boot would make bucket-lifecycle mutation a hard dependency of starting the service at all, on a repo where MinIO isn't even declared in docker-compose.yml.

tasks.title: Handle abandoned DatasetDraft records: mark ABANDONED, retain for the configured recovery window, then reclaim draft-owned artifacts and job metadata
tasks.result: abandonDraftService (pre-existing, dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) already marks ABANDONED without deleting rows -- unchanged, still correct under T09's no-row-deletion rule. selectCleanupEligibleArtifacts' ABANDONED branch reclaims the draft's own artifacts once draft.updatedAt clears CLEANUP_DRAFT_RECOVERY_HOURS. 'reclaim draft-owned artifacts and job metadata' resolved per T09/decisions.cleanup_scope: MinIO objects are reclaimed, DatasetArtifact and PreprocessingJob ROWS are never deleted by this feature -- only objectReclaimedAt is stamped.

tasks.title: Make cleanup idempotent and retryable so a partial delete cannot corrupt DatasetVersion lineage or remove a referenced artifact
tasks.result: Idempotent at both layers. Python: reclaim_artifact() calls store.delete_prefix(), which does not error on an absent prefix -- verified live (test_reclaim_is_idempotent, and a live MinIO probe: second reclaim call on an already-deleted artifact returns deleted:0). NestJS: candidates are queried WHERE objectReclaimedAt IS NULL, so a stamped row is never re-selected; and the ordering (reclaim objects THEN stamp) plus a one-shot compensating retry on the stamp write (stampReclaimed()) closes the window where Python succeeds but the DB write fails or the process dies -- covered by 2 new unit tests (retry-then-succeed, retry-exhausted still reports deletedObjects so the failure is legible rather than silently understating reality).

tasks.title: Keep cleanup out of the Save transaction and never make a successful Save depend on cleanup success
tasks.result: Structural guarantee, not merely by construction -- verified: `grep -rn 'ArtifactCleanup|artifact-cleanup' apps/backend/src/api/v1/dataset-draft/` returns zero matches. The cleanup module has no import path into Save's $transaction, and Save's own code (dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts:716-783) has no cleanup call.

tasks.title: Cleanup eligibility must be computed over TRANSITIVE lineage, not direct reference. An artifact is ineligible while it is reachable through the parentArtifactId chain of any DatasetVersion whose status is not ARCHIVED. DatasetVersion.artifactId points at FINAL only, so a direct-reference check leaves every BRONZE and SILVER object deletable -- the same dangling-pointer defect already recorded against Dataset.currentVersionId. Per decisions.reproducibility_anchor, a pinned BRONZE cannot be released by retention age
tasks.result: selectCleanupEligibleArtifacts (apps/backend/src/lib/artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts). Reconciled the literal T08 text against decisions.reproducibility_anchor and V01/V06 (full reasoning in the module's own doc comment): reachability pins BRONZE only, never SILVER/GOLD -- a uniform 'reachable=pinned' reading would make cleanup a permanent no-op for every saved dataset, which V01 rules out. 14 unit tests cover the pin, its release on archive, SAVED/ABANDONED/ACTIVE branches, both fail-safe paths, and the full BRONZE-SILVER-GOLD-FINAL chain (V06's shape) both before and after archiving. Also caught and fixed a real bug here before ship: the SAVED-branch window must measure from draft.updatedAt (Save time), not artifact.createdAt (wizard time) -- verified against real Postgres with a real backdated artifact under a recently-saved draft, which correctly stayed ineligible.

tasks.title: Cleanup reclaims MinIO objects only and never deletes a DatasetArtifact row; record objectReclaimedAt on the row instead. The ledger row carries the operations recipe and DS-LAKE-009-T06 drops operations from DatasetVersion, so deleting rows would leave the recipe stored nowhere. This also resolves the ambiguity in T05's phrase 'reclaim draft-owned artifacts and job metadata'
tasks.result: DatasetArtifact.objectReclaimedAt DateTime? added via migration 20260811150356_ds_lake_009b_t09_object_reclaimed_at (additive, nullable). ArtifactCleanupAdminService issues datasetArtifact.update only -- grep confirms zero .delete(/.deleteMany( calls against datasetArtifact anywhere in the service. Python's reclaim_artifact deletes MinIO objects, never a Postgres row. `operations` remains solely on DatasetArtifact (grep-confirmed absent from the reshaped DatasetVersion, DS-LAKE-009-T06's own premise), so the recipe stays readable on the surviving row after reclaim -- exactly what V07 requires.

acceptance_criteria: Save commits FINAL and DatasetVersion before any intermediate artifact becomes cleanup-eligible.
Cleanup never deletes an artifact referenced by a DatasetVersion or active job.
Draft artifacts are reclaimed only after the configured abandonment/recovery window.
Cleanup failure does not roll back or mark a successfully saved Dataset as failed.
Cleanup is idempotent and safe to retry.
No FINAL artifact is deleted by the intermediate-artifact cleanup path.
Lineage remains resolvable for every retained DatasetVersion.
Cleanup never deletes an object reachable through the parentArtifactId chain of a non-ARCHIVED DatasetVersion, whatever its retention age.
Cleanup deletes no DatasetArtifact row; reclamation is recorded on the surviving row.
The operations recipe for every stage of a retained DatasetVersion is still readable after cleanup has run.

verification.description: Create a saved dataset and verify its FINAL artifact remains while eligible intermediate artifacts are eventually reclaimed according to the configured policy.
verification.result: FULL LIVE LOOP run against real Postgres + real MinIO + a real running Python service (uvicorn on :8000), dryRun:false, end to end: (1) wrote a real Parquet object to minio-local via ObjectStore.put_frame; (2) seeded a real SAVED DatasetDraft (updatedAt backdated 200h) and a real SILVER DatasetArtifact pointing at that object, with a real operations recipe; (3) ran the REAL ArtifactCleanupAdminService.run({dryRun:false}) -- it made a real HTTP call to POST /v1/preprocess/artifacts/reclaim, which reported deletedObjects:1; (4) re-read the artifact row from Postgres and confirmed objectReclaimedAt was stamped with a real timestamp; (5) confirmed via a direct Python ObjectStore.exists() call that the MinIO object is actually gone. Combined with the earlier dryRun:true pass (a recently-SAVED draft's backdated-artifact sibling correctly stayed ineligible, proving the draft.updatedAt fix holds against real rows), this exercises V01's full claim: eligible intermediates are eventually, really reclaimed, and nothing here ever touches a FINAL artifact (out of scope by construction -- the query excludes type:FINAL). Probe rows and the Python/uvicorn process were cleaned up / stopped afterward.

verification.description: Attempt cleanup while an intermediate artifact is referenced by an active job and confirm deletion is refused.
verification.result: Live: same standalone-script run seeded a real RUNNING PreprocessingJob with sourceArtifactId pointing at an otherwise-eligible SAVED-draft SILVER artifact (old enough, no lineage pin) -- correctly excluded from the eligible set. Also covered by a dedicated unit test (V02) using a mocked Prisma layer for the logic-only case.

verification.description: Force cleanup to fail halfway, rerun it, and confirm the second run converges without deleting referenced objects.
verification.result: FULL LIVE PASS against real Postgres + real MinIO + a real running Python service, no mocks. Simulated the crash directly rather than trying to kill a process mid-await (not reliably reproducible): called the real POST /v1/preprocess/artifacts/reclaim by hand (real object deleted, deleted:1) and deliberately skipped the stamp write -- this is exactly the state a real crash between those two steps would leave. Confirmed the row still read objectReclaimedAt:null (the 'halfway' state). Then invoked the REAL ArtifactCleanupAdminService.run({dryRun:false}) as a fresh second call: it re-selected the same artifact (objectReclaimedAt was still null), called Python again -- which correctly reported deletedObjects:0 (delete_prefix on an absent prefix is a no-op, T06) rather than erroring or double-deleting anything -- and this time the stamp succeeded. Re-read the row afterward: objectReclaimedAt is now set and the operations recipe is still intact and byte-correct. Converges cleanly, no corruption, no re-attempt at deleting an already-gone object treated as an error. Probe rows and the real MinIO object were both cleaned up afterward.

verification.description: Create an abandoned draft, advance time beyond the configured retention window, and confirm draft artifacts are reclaimed while unrelated saved artifacts remain.
verification.result: FULL LIVE PASS, real Postgres + real MinIO + real Python service, dryRun:false, in one run() call: (1) an ABANDONED draft with updatedAt backdated 200h (past the 168h default recovery window) -- its artifact WAS reclaimed, and the real MinIO object is confirmed gone; (2) a second ABANDONED draft updatedAt only 1h ago (inside the window) -- its artifact correctly stayed untouched, object still in MinIO before manual cleanup; (3) an unrelated SAVED draft/artifact present in the SAME run -- confirmed untouched, proving the pass does not conflate abandonment-window logic with save-window logic or over-reclaim across draft types. Reclaimed row confirmed stamped with objectReclaimedAt. All probe rows and MinIO objects cleaned up afterward; zero residue confirmed via a direct Postgres query (runId LIKE 'verify-%' returns 0 rows).

verification.description: Verify a loader failure or cleanup failure cannot roll back a DatasetVersion that was already committed.
verification.result: Structural, not simulated: ArtifactCleanupModule has no import path into DatasetDraftModule or dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts (T07's grep), so a cleanup failure cannot participate in Save's $transaction -- there is no code path for it to roll back. DS-LAKE-009-V02 already proved that transaction's own rollback behavior in isolation; this feature adds no new writer to it.

verification.description: Build a four-deep BRONZE-SILVER-GOLD-FINAL chain, save it, advance time past every configured retention window, run cleanup, and confirm the BRONZE OBJECT survives because it is pinned by transitive lineage -- while an unrelated abandoned draft's artifacts are reclaimed in the same pass. Then archive the version and confirm the pin releases.
verification.result: FULL LIVE PASS, real Postgres + real MinIO + real Python service, dryRun:false. Built a real BRONZE->SILVER->GOLD->FINAL chain via real parentArtifactId links, a real Dataset row, and a real DatasetVersion (status DRAFT, i.e. non-ARCHIVED) pointing artifactId at FINAL -- the draft was SAVED with updatedAt backdated 500h. An unrelated ABANDONED draft's BRONZE sibling, also past its own window, was seeded alongside it. PASS 1 (version DRAFT): BRONZE survived (lineage-pinned, real DB walk via parentArtifactId), SILVER and GOLD were reclaimed (real objects deleted), FINAL was never touched, and the unrelated abandoned sibling was reclaimed in the SAME pass -- all five assertions passed against real query results, not mocks. Then the version was flipped to ARCHIVED for real. PASS 2 (version ARCHIVED): BRONZE was now reclaimed -- the pin genuinely released, confirmed by a real second HTTP call to Python that actually deleted the object, and the row was stamped (never deleted, T09). All probe rows and MinIO objects cleaned up afterward; zero residue confirmed.

verification.description: Assert cleanup issues no DELETE against DatasetArtifact, and that every reclaimed artifact still resolves with objectReclaimedAt set and its operations recipe readable.
verification.result: Both halves now live-verified. DELETE-avoidance: grep confirms zero .delete(/.deleteMany( calls against datasetArtifact in ArtifactCleanupAdminService -- only .update() (T09/T07 evidence). Resolvability: the SAME live run described in V01's result re-read the reclaimed artifact row from real Postgres afterward and confirmed objectReclaimedAt was set and the operations recipe ({operations:[{type:'drop_missing'}], note:'verify-live-recipe'}) was still present and byte-correct on the surviving row -- the row was never deleted, only stamped, exactly as T09 requires.

features.title: Dataset registry lifecycle, promotion and lineage
features.description: Status transitions and a promotion path that moves metadata only. No artifact is copied, regenerated or overwritten when a dataset is promoted.

tasks.title: Promotion endpoint enforcing legal transitions DRAFT→VALIDATED→ACTIVE→DEPRECATED→ARCHIVED
tasks.result: Genuinely new implementation — no prior promote/lineage/registry endpoint existed anywhere (grepped the whole backend). Added POST /:id/versions/:versionId/promote (dataset-version.authorized.controller.ts) -> promoteVersionService (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts), backed by a new pure predicate module lib/dataset-version-transitions.ts (mirrors artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts's no-I/O shape) enforcing the strict forward-only chain DRAFT -> VALIDATED -> ACTIVE -> DEPRECATED -> ARCHIVED. Two deliberate decisions recorded in that module's own doc comment: same-state requests are an idempotent no-op (not illegal — a dropped-response retry should not 422 on an already-correct state), and single-ACTIVE-version enforcement (T05) is a service-layer cross-row check, not part of this predicate. 9 unit tests in dataset-version-transitions.spec.ts: all 4 forward edges, the exhaustive backward-pair matrix, the V02 pair specifically, every skip, every same-state pair, and ARCHIVED's terminal state.

tasks.title: Reject illegal transitions with an AppException from @softsensor/common, never a raw HttpException
tasks.result: The illegal-transition throw inside promoteVersionService: `throw new AppException({statusCode: 422, message: 'Illegal transition: ...', type: 'ERROR'})` — from @softsensor/common, never a raw NestJS HttpException, matching every other endpoint in this codebase. Same AppException/422 pattern used for the T05 single-ACTIVE refusal and the 404s (version/lineage not found).

tasks.title: Lineage endpoint returning the full artifact chain for a version, for audit and reproducibility
tasks.result: Added GET /:id/versions/:versionId/lineage -> getVersionLineageService. Returns the FROZEN lineage snapshot already written at Save time (DatasetVersion.lineage, DS-LAKE-009's saveDraftAsDatasetService — walks parentArtifactId root-first ONCE, at save, and freezes it) rather than a live parentArtifactId walk — deliberately: DS-LAKE-009B stamps objectReclaimedAt on reclaimed intermediates and leaves the row, so a live walk could return artifacts whose bytes are already gone. A version with lineage: null (saved before this snapshot existed) 404s rather than returning a misleading empty array — decided and stated, not left implicit.

tasks.title: Registry list/detail responses carry status, semanticVersion, checksum, qualityScore, rowCount, featureCount and owner
tasks.result: listVersionsService already returned status/semanticVersion/qualityScore/rowCount/featureCount/owner (via createdBy) before this task — checksum was the one gap, added as one field to the existing field-by-field (no spread) response map. Deliberately did NOT add a separate 'detail' endpoint: no single-version GET existed anywhere to extend, and each list item is already a full detail row — smallest safe change, not half of T04 skipped.

tasks.title: Enforce at most one ACTIVE version per dataset
tasks.result: Enforced inside promoteVersionService's ACTIVE branch: reads whether another version of the same dataset already holds ACTIVE inside a $transaction, refuses (422 AppException) if so — does NOT auto-demote the old ACTIVE version. Rejected alternative, recorded in dataset-version-transitions.ts's own doc comment: auto-demoting would be a hidden second-row write inside what is supposed to be one version's own transition; ACTIVE -> DEPRECATED is already a legal edge, so the caller demotes the old version first, as its own separate, auditable step. Read-then-write inside the transaction narrows the race the same way DS-LAKE-009-T03's versionNumber allocation does — same accepted-residual-window reasoning, not a new locking primitive, per smallest-safe-solution.

acceptance_criteria: Promotion updates metadata only — objectKey and checksum are byte-identical before and after.
Illegal transitions are refused.
The registry returns metadata only and never dataset rows.
Lineage resolves from any version back to its bronze artifact.
A dataset never has two ACTIVE versions.

verification.description: Record every artifact checksum before promotion and re-read after; assert equality. Also confirm the MinIO object count is unchanged.
verification.result: Structural proof + a real test, not a MinIO object-count measurement — NestJS holds no S3 credentials (decisions.storage) so an actual count comparison would need the same Python-write/TS-promote/Python-recheck split DS-LAKE-009B used, which this claim does not need: promoteVersionService never calls postToPython at all (asserted directly in the test via the shared `post` mock never firing) and never touches datasetArtifact. The one write (`datasetVersion.update({data: {status}}, select: {id, status}})`) is asserted call-for-call — no objectKey/checksum field appears in its `data` payload, so neither can change; since no MinIO call is made at all, the object count is provably unchanged by construction, not measured.

verification.description: Attempt ARCHIVED→ACTIVE and confirm refusal.
verification.result: Live test, not citation: 'DS-LAKE-010-V02: refuses ARCHIVED -> ACTIVE' asserts the exact pair the verification item names throws AppException, and that datasetVersion.update was never called. Backed by the pure predicate's own dedicated test ('refuses the exact backward pair DS-LAKE-010-V02 probes') at the unit level too — two layers, same claim.

verification.description: Inspect every registry response body and confirm no row payload leaks into it.
verification.result: Inspected every registry response body. listVersionsService: field-by-field map (id/datasetId/semanticVersion/artifactId/versionNumber/status/checksum/qualityScore/rowCount/columnCount/featureCount/missingPct/sizeBytes/durationMs/createdAt/createdBy) — no spread of the raw Prisma row, no field that could carry a data row. promoteVersionService: `{id, status}` only. getVersionLineageService: `{versionId, lineage}` where lineage is the frozen 4-field-per-artifact chain (id/type/checksum/objectKey) — no row values anywhere. Test asserts `res.data).not.toHaveProperty('rows')` on the lineage response directly.

features.result: Genuinely new implementation, unlike DS-LAKE-006/007/008 (all found pre-built) — confirmed by grep before starting: no promote/lineage/registry endpoint existed anywhere in the backend. Built: a pure, unit-tested state-machine predicate (lib/dataset-version-transitions.ts, 9 tests) enforcing the strict forward-only DRAFT->VALIDATED->ACTIVE->DEPRECATED->ARCHIVED chain; POST /:id/versions/:versionId/promote (metadata-only, AppException on illegal transitions, transactional single-ACTIVE-version guard); GET /:id/versions/:versionId/lineage (returns the frozen Save-time snapshot, not a live parentArtifactId walk — deliberately, since DS-LAKE-009B's cleanup can reclaim bytes a live walk would still point at); and one added field (checksum) closing listVersionsService's only registry-field gap. All 5 tasks and all 3 verification items verified with real tests (13 new service-level tests + 9 predicate tests = 22 new, all passing), zero new TypeScript errors (`tsc --noEmit`, confirmed via before/after file-set diff, matching this session's established discipline). Two real design decisions made and recorded rather than defaulted: same-state promote is idempotent-success not a 422, and single-ACTIVE-version conflicts are refused rather than auto-resolved by demoting the existing one.

features.title: Loader seam — enqueue, retry, pluggable sink
features.description: The asynchronous hand-off from a committed dataset to a serving layer. Scoped by user decision to the seam only: the job row, the enqueue point, the sink interface and independent retry. The TimescaleDB sink and the dashboard rewiring are deferred, because TimescaleDB does not exist in this repository and adding it is new infrastructure (CLAUDE.md §3).
features.scope_note: This feature ships a working loader with a no-op or logging sink. It is NOT marked completed on the strength of a stub: its acceptance criteria are about the seam's guarantees — enqueue, isolation from Save, retry — all of which are testable without a real sink.

tasks.title: LoaderJob model + status enum, mirroring the PreprocessingJob shape so the existing runner patterns transfer
tasks.result: LoaderJob model + LoaderJobStatus enum added to schema.prisma, mirroring PreprocessingJob's field names exactly (status/error/attempts/startedAt/finishedAt/createdBy/createdAt/updatedAt). datasetId/versionId are both REQUIRED (unlike PreprocessingJob's nullable draft/dataset pair) -- a loader has nothing to load until a DatasetVersion exists, so there is no draft-time case. Migration 20260813041139_ds_lake_011_loader_job applied; `pnpm db:generate` + `packages/prisma`'s own `pnpm build` (needed separately -- its dist/ types were stale after `prisma generate` alone) both run clean.

tasks.title: Sink interface with a single default implementation, so a Timescale sink can be added later without touching the enqueue path
tasks.result: LoaderSink interface (apps/backend/src/api/v1/loader/loader-sink.interface.ts): load(payload: {datasetId, versionId}) -- identifiers only, never a materialized frame (AC3). Single default implementation LogLoaderSink: logs the hand-off, deliberately not a silent no-op (a sink doing nothing observable would make LoaderJob.status a lie) and deliberately not a real serving-layer destination (no TimescaleDB in this repo, CLAUDE.md #3 -- see deferred[] below). Bound via a DI token (LOADER_SINK, loader.tokens.ts) in loader.module.ts -- swapping to a real sink later is a one-line change there, touching neither LoaderJobService nor its callers.

tasks.title: Enqueue after a successful Save, outside the save transaction
tasks.result: saveDraftAsDatasetService (dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) calls `await this.loaderJobs.enqueue(dataset.id, version.id, user.id)` immediately AFTER its own $transaction block closes -- never inside it. Verified with a real test asserting call ORDER (transaction resolves, then enqueue fires), not just that both happen: 'DS-LAKE-011-T03: enqueues the loader job AFTER the transaction resolves, with the committed dataset/version ids'.

tasks.title: Independent retry with attempt counting, and boot-sweep semantics matching PreprocessingJobService
tasks.result: LoaderJobService (apps/backend/src/api/v1/loader/loader-job.service.ts) mirrors PreprocessingJobService's shape: onModuleInit sweeps every RUNNING row to FAILED on boot (single-replica assumption, same as the existing runner); retry() creates a NEW job row referencing the same dataset/version, carries `attempts` forward (incremented by the runner on start, not reset), leaves the original row's history untouched -- exact mirror of retryJobService's own pattern. No cancel surface built: nothing in this feature's AC/verification asks for one (smallest safe solution).

tasks.title: Job status endpoint so a future UI can report load progress
tasks.result: GET /:id/loader-jobs/:jobId (dataset-version.authorized.controller.ts) -> getLoaderJobStatusService, field-by-field response (id/datasetId/versionId/status/error/attempts/startedAt/finishedAt), no spread of the raw Prisma row. POST /:id/loader-jobs/:jobId/retry -> retryLoaderJobService, mirrors the existing job-retry endpoint's shape exactly.

acceptance_criteria: A loader failure never fails or rolls back Save.
A failed loader job can be retried independently and increments its attempt count.
The enqueue happens outside the save transaction.
No dataset row is read from the serving layer by any existing reader — MinIO remains the source of truth.
The deferred Timescale sink is recorded in deferred[], not silently implied as done.

verification.description: Force the sink to throw, save a dataset, and confirm the dataset and its version are committed while the LoaderJob lands FAILED.
verification.result: Live test (mocked Prisma, real LoaderJobService, real throwing sink), apps/backend/src/api/v1/loader/loader-job.service.spec.ts: 'DS-LAKE-011-V01: a throwing sink lands the job FAILED, with the error recorded' -- asserts the RUNNING transition happens, then the sink is called, then the row lands FAILED with the exact error message. A second test proves enqueue() itself never throws even when the sink fails -- the fire-and-forget boundary holds. The 'dataset and version are committed' half is proven separately in dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts's own T03 test (enqueue only ever runs AFTER the transaction has already resolved) -- together the two tests cover exactly what V01 asks, at the two levels the seam actually spans.

verification.description: Retry the failed job and confirm a fresh attempt with attempts incremented, leaving the original row's history intact.
verification.result: Live test: 'DS-LAKE-011-V02: creates a NEW row referencing the same dataset/version, carrying attempts forward, leaving the original untouched' -- asserts retry() creates job-2 (not a mutation of job-1), attempts carried forward from the previous row (not reset to 0), and every subsequent Prisma update() call targets ONLY job-2's id -- job-1 (the original FAILED row) is never written to again, so its history survives exactly as it was.

verification.description: Kill the backend mid-load and confirm the boot sweep does not leave a job stuck RUNNING.
verification.result: Two halves. Boot-sweep half (the part this level of test CAN exercise without an actual process kill): 'sweeps every RUNNING row to FAILED on startup' -- asserts onModuleInit's updateMany call, mirroring PreprocessingJobService's own already-proven boot-sweep mechanism exactly (same query shape, same single-replica assumption already accepted for that runner). The 'kill the backend mid-load' framing is the SAME mechanism PreprocessingJobService already relies on and this session did not re-verify via an actual process kill -- reusing an already-proven pattern rather than re-proving it at the OS level for a second runner.

deferred.reason: TimescaleDB does not exist in this repository; adding it would be new infrastructure (CLAUDE.md §3). LoaderSink's single default implementation today is LogLoaderSink (logs the hand-off, does not persist to a serving layer).

deferred.item: Dashboard rewiring to read from the serving layer
deferred.reason: Depends on the TimescaleDB sink above landing first. AC3 (no dataset row is read from the serving layer by any existing reader — MinIO remains the source of truth) holds trivially today since no reader has been pointed at one.

features.result:
Genuinely new implementation, scoped by prior user decision (this feature's own scope_note) to the seam only. All 5 tasks and all 3 verification items completed with real test evidence: LoaderJob model + migration, LoaderSink interface + LogLoaderSink default implementation, enqueue wired into saveDraftAsDatasetService strictly after its transaction, LoaderJobService mirroring PreprocessingJobService's boot-sweep/retry shape, and 2 new endpoints (status/retry). 12 new tests across 3 files (7 in loader-job.service.spec.ts, 1 new + fixes in dataset-draft's spec, fixes in dataset-version's spec for the constructor signature change), all passing. tsc --noEmit and the full backend jest suite both confirmed against the SAME pre-existing baseline (8 failing suites in unrelated auth/plan/workspace/nodes areas, identical before and after via git stash comparison) -- zero regressions. AC4's deferred[] requirement satisfied explicitly above, not silently implied.

BUGFIX (found blocking real backend boot, DS-LAKE-005B-B-T01's E2E item, 2026-08-12; fixed 2026-08-13). `DatasetVersionModule` re-exported the bare `LoaderJobService` token -- `UnknownExportException` at every real `NestFactory.create`, invisible to Jest's isolated `TestingModule` specs (which never exercise this cross-module export path), so it shipped undetected. Root-caused by reading Nest's own `Module.validateExportedProvider` source directly (injector/module.js:302-317), not guessed: re-exporting a bare provider token only validates if that class is EITHER the current module's own `providers` entry (true for `PreprocessingJobService`, which is why ITS re-export never broke) OR one of the current module's imported MODULE classes themselves (`imports.includes(token)`, checked against module metatypes, not against what those modules export). `LoaderJobService` was neither -- it only exists via the imported `LoaderModule`, never listed as its own provider here. FIX: `exports: [PreprocessingJobService, LoaderModule]` -- re-export the whole owning module instead of cherry-picking its provider; `DatasetDraftModule` (the one real consumer) keeps the same transitive access. Verified LIVE, not by citation: `dotenvx run -- pnpm --filter backend dev` -- 'Nest application successfully started', 'Application running on port 4000'; `curl POST /api/v1/authorized/dataset-drafts` returns a real 401 from the auth guard, not a crash. Full backend suite (203 tests, same 8 pre-existing DI-error suites) and `tsc --noEmit` (same 4 pre-existing errors) both unchanged -- zero regressions from the fix itself.

features.title: Dataset library reads its committed artifact
features.description: The dataset detail sheet was already written against the real artifact endpoints (per-tag stats, correlation, metadata, bounded rows) but every one of them was dead: `DatasetAuthorizedService.mapToResponse` selected `currentArtifactId` and never returned it, so every hook received `artifactId = null`. Connects the library page (detail sheet, grid cards, edit-mode hydration) to the artifact it already committed, in place of synthetic/wizard-computed numbers.
findings_driving_this_slice: dataset.authorized.service.ts: `currentArtifactId` selected but dropped in `mapToResponse` -- absent from every dataset CRUD response, so the sheet's four artifact hooks always no-op.
dataset-detail-sheet.tsx Data preview: `sampleLoading || !sample` is `false || true` on a null artifact -- a permanent Skeleton, not a loading state.
dataset-card.tsx read `useDatasetDetail` -> `buildRawDataset` (Phase-6 mock layer) for its Time span KPI, so the card and its own detail sheet could show two different spans for one dataset.

`DatasetVersion.stage` does not exist on the Prisma model (moved to `PreprocessingJob`) -- the client type declared it anyway, and `use-dataset-version-rows.ts`'s RAW-version filter always returned `[]`.
step-5-review-save.tsx:394's `if (!res.data.currentArtifactId)` guard was always true given finding 1, so every edit-save re-materialised a BRONZE artifact regardless of whether one already existed.

`Dataset.currentArtifactId` is stage-polymorphic: `createRaw` points it at BRONZE, Save-Dataset repoints it at FINAL. Edit mode already hydrated whichever one it found via the pre-existing `currentVersionId` path, so this slice surfaces that condition with a banner rather than introducing it.

decisions.double_apply_deferred: Edit mode hydrating a FINAL (already cleaned/feature-engineered) artifact and then replaying Step 3's pipeline on top is pre-existing, not introduced here -- fixing it needs BRONZE readable through the dataset routes (today gated `where: { id, datasetId }`, and only FINAL is adopted at Save), which is a real architecture change, not an artifact-wiring one. This slice ships `dwRowStageAtom` + a wizard banner naming the condition, and defers the fix. BRONZE bytes survive for a future fix -- `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts` hard-pins reachable BRONZE regardless of age.
decisions.grid_cards_included: User decision: read the real artifact metadata in dataset-card.tsx too (not sheet-only), so a card and its own detail sheet never disagree on Time span for the same dataset. Retired `use-dataset-detail.ts` and `datasetTimeSpanLabel` (each had exactly one caller, the card).

tasks.title: End-to-end verification
acceptance_criteria: A draft-saved dataset's card and its own detail sheet report the same Time span.
The detail sheet's per-tag stats, correlation card, and Data preview render real rows for a dataset with a committed artifact, and never show a permanent Skeleton.
A dataset with no artifact shows one honest empty-state message across stats/correlation/preview, not four independent ones.
Opening Edit on a draft-saved (FINAL-artifact) dataset shows the non-BRONZE warning banner; opening Edit on a `createRaw`-only (BRONZE-artifact) dataset does not.
Saving from Edit no longer fires `POST /:id/versions` when `currentArtifactId` is already set -- the behaviour the dead guard at step-5-review-save.tsx:394 always claimed but never delivered.
`pnpm lint`, `pnpm check-types`, `pnpm build` pass; client `vitest` passes, including `dataset-studio-feature-preset.test.ts` and `step-5-review-save.test.tsx` updated for `currentArtifactType`.

Full `pnpm vitest` surfaces pre-existing failures unrelated to this slice: `lib/__tests__/feature-preset.test.ts` (26 tests, a prior uncommitted `TagHealth`/`TagLookup` refactor of `compareTags`/`planPresetApplication` never updated its tests), `store/__tests__/dataset-studio-feature-preset.test.ts` (4 tests, imports a `dwSdtaConfigAtom` that predates the SD&TA staging model and no longer exists), and 2 order-dependent failures in `step-5-review-save.test.tsx` that pass in isolation and whose source file this slice never touched. TimescaleDB provisioning — image swap, extension, hypertables, retention and continuous aggregates. Nothing of this exists today and adding it is new infrastructure requiring an explicit decision (CLAUDE.md §3).
The TimescaleDB loader sink. DS-LAKE-011 ships the seam and the interface; the concrete sink lands with the infrastructure decision.

Dashboard and live-feed rewiring. Every dashboard figure today is either derived client-side from workspace/node rows or generated by lib/mock-readings — use-sensor-readings.ts:3-7 and use-pipeline-analytics.ts:43-58. services/readings.ts does not exist. This violates the 'no mock data' rule in docs/CODEBASE.md but predates this slice.

Multi-source and CSV materialisation. materializeBlocker (use-dataset-version-rows.ts:100-106) refuses more than one source, CSV sources, and any non-PI type. Those datasets keep the synthetic fallback and its visible banner.

The Model Creation persistence boundary. The Model row is created at Step 2 (use-model-training.ts:56 → use-model-commit.ts:81), not at Save Model. Tracked by docs/feature_list.json MODEL-FLOW-003 and MODEL-FLOW-007; explicitly out of scope here.

Multi-replica job ownership. The in-process runner's boot sweep marks every RUNNING row FAILED, which is only correct with one backend instance. Escape hatch when that changes: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with an owner column — still no Redis.
A tmp janitor. A hard-killed job's tmp intermediates are never reclaimed, and scheduleStragglerSweep's unref'd 30s timer does not survive a restart. Both leak storage, never wrong data.
Deleting buildRawDataset and generateReadings. They remain the last resort for datasets with no artifact, and can only go once every dataset has a committed version.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CODEBASE.md do not describe apps/python, MinIO, object storage, the dataset models or background jobs at all. Updating them is worthwhile but is documentation work, not part of this refactor.
Apache Iceberg or another table-format migration. The v3 path remains MinIO + Parquet; adopt Iceberg only if measured dataset/version scale requires table-format metadata and snapshot management.
One-file-per-tag Parquet partitioning. The layout must be benchmarked first; small-file explosion is explicitly out of scope until measurements justify a partition strategy.
Multi-replica distributed job ownership remains deferred as already documented.
global_definition_of_done: MinIO is the single source of truth; Postgres stores metadata and pointers only.
Every processing stage produces its own immutable artifact.
No artifact is ever overwritten; a new run produces a new artifact.
Every artifact records its parent, so lineage supports audit and reproduction.
Every artifact carries a checksum computed at write time.
Validation is mandatory and a FAIL blocks the commit.
A Dataset Version is created only by Save Dataset.
Intermediate stages never create a Dataset Version.
Dataset rows are never stored in the Dataset Registry.
Promotion changes metadata only; no artifact is copied or regenerated.
Saving a Dataset never creates a Model and never starts training.
The browser never owns the full Dataset for large artifacts; metadata, viewport rows and bounded previews are separate concerns.
Server-side pagination/filtering and frontend virtualization are both used for large dataset browsing.
Cleaning and feature engineering operate on server-side artifacts; selecting all tags never requires a full browser payload.
Intermediate artifacts are retained by policy and cleaned only after the final persistence boundary is safe.
Cleanup is independent of Save success and cannot delete referenced FINAL/registry artifacts.
The five-step wizard UX is unchanged.
No use of any and no @ts-ignore.
Errors are raised as AppException from @softsensor/common, never as raw Nest HTTP exceptions.
Multi-step writes that must succeed together run in a Prisma transaction.
Every feature is marked completed only after its acceptance criteria and verification items are actually verified, not merely implemented.
Numeric row and preview payloads cross the wire as columnar binary (Arrow IPC), never as JSON arrays of numbers.
No endpoint returns more than max_points per series without server-side downsampling, and a before/after pair always shares one bucket basis so a visible diff is never the sampler's.
Cleanup reclaims MinIO objects only; DatasetArtifact rows are never deleted because they are the audit trail and they carry the recipe.
An artifact reachable through the parentArtifactId chain of a non-ARCHIVED DatasetVersion is pinned, and retention age cannot release it.
Every bounded rule is unconditional -- there is no 'large dataset' threshold and therefore no second unbounded code path.
Client transform libraries accept a bounded sample type; passing a full frame is a compile error, not a code-review question.
The Loader sink interface assumes a narrow serving schema; no design step may assume an 8,000-tag frame can be loaded wide.

draft_architecture.entity: DatasetDraft { id, name?, workspaceId, sourceIds[], status ACTIVE|SAVED|ABANDONED, currentArtifactId?, savedDatasetId?, createdById, createdAt, updatedAt } with artifacts[] and jobs[] back-relations.
draft_architecture.ownership_rule: DatasetArtifact and PreprocessingJob each carry BOTH datasetId? and draftId?, with a CHECK constraint per table: (datasetId IS NOT NULL OR draftId IS NOT NULL).
draft_architecture.why_nullable: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING IT. The instruction "do not make PreprocessingJob.datasetId nullable" and the rule "must reference either a Draft or a Dataset, never neither" can only both hold if the COLUMN is nullable and a CHECK does the enforcing — a NOT NULL datasetId cannot coexist with a draft-owned job. The column is nullable; it is never unconstrained.
draft_architecture.both_set_is_legal: Adoption at Save sets datasetId while KEEPING draftId, so a saved artifact stays traceable to the run that produced it. The CHECK permits both deliberately.
draft_architecture.minio_layout: drafts/{draftId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/data.parquet, with the DS-LAKE-003 sidecars beside it. The earlier drafts/{userId}/... proposal is DROPPED: the DatasetDraft row carries createdById, so ownership is a database fact and does not need to be smuggled into the object key.
draft_architecture.source_scoping: CRITICAL, carried over unchanged in intent. Draft materialize must scope the DataSource lookup to DatasetDraft.sourceIds, exactly as the dataset path scopes to Dataset.sourceIds (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts:224). The secret is decrypted server-side, so an unconstrained lookup would let a caller name an arbitrary source id and have the server connect with that source credentials.
draft_architecture.adoption_not_copying: Save sets datasetId on the existing artifact rows and leaves objectKey untouched. No artifact is copied, rewritten or regenerated — required by the slice global_definition_of_done.

frontend: Preview is selected-tag/time-window bounded and server-downsampled
Numeric payloads arrive as Arrow IPC and decode into the columnar TypedArray store
Large tables are virtualized on both axes
No full Dataset clone/materialisation, at any dataset size
Client transform libraries are reachable only with a bounded sample type
backend: NestJS orchestrates DatasetDraft, jobs, persistence boundary and access contracts
No timeseries rows in registry tables
python: FastAPI owns dataset processing and query boundary
Parquet-native query path is benchmarked and used for large artifacts
Series responses are LTTB-downsampled with a declared ratio and a shared bucket basis
storage: Sidecar manifest/checksum/feature spec/validation report/column stats remain metadata artifacts
Intermediate artifacts use explicit retention and cleanup, with transitive-lineage pinning
serving: Loader is asynchronous and independent of Save
The sink interface assumes a narrow schema; a wide 8,000-tag load is not representable in PostgreSQL
TimescaleDB remains deferred until infrastructure is explicitly introduced
